text: 四十年来家国，三千里地山河
pinyin: sì shí nián lái jiā guó, sān qiān lǐ dì shān hé
literal: forty · years · since · home-and-state, three · thousand · li · land · mountains · rivers
natural: for forty years a kingdom, three thousand li of mountains and rivers

meaning.en: Li Yu's opening lines, recalling the realm of Southern Tang that he ruled for decades and has now lost.
meaning.zh: 李煜词的开篇，回顾南唐立国数十年、疆土三千里的往昔，如今都已失去。

equivalents: a kingdom once mine, now lost
the land I held, and lost

examples.zh: 读到“四十年来家国，三千里地山河”，才懂亡国之君的哀痛。
examples.en: Reading 'forty years a kingdom, three thousand li of rivers and hills', one grasps the grief of a ruler who lost his state.

examples.zh: 导游念起“四十年来家国，三千里地山河”，感叹南唐旧事。
examples.en: The guide recited 'forty years a kingdom, three thousand li of mountains and rivers' and sighed over the fate of Southern Tang.

origin.source: 李煜《破阵子·四十年来家国》

story.en: Li Yu (937-978), last ruler of the Southern Tang, wrote this lyric in captivity after the state fell to the Song; the lines open 'Forty years a kingdom, three thousand li of mountains and rivers'.
story.zh: 李煜（937—978）南唐后主，国亡被俘后作此词，开篇即“四十年来家国，三千里地山河”。

date.zh: 南唐亡后 · 北宋 · 约977—978年
date.en: after the fall of Southern Tang, Northern Song, c. 977–978

usage.en: Quoted when speaking of Li Yu or of lost homelands. Literary and elegiac. The 'forty years' is a round figure for the Southern Tang's history.
usage.zh: 谈论李煜或失去的故国时引用，书面、哀婉。“四十年”为南唐立国年数的约数。

text: 我住长江头，君住长江尾
pinyin: wǒ zhù cháng jiāng tóu, jūn zhù cháng jiāng wěi
literal: I · live · Yangtze · head, you · live · Yangtze · tail
natural: I live at the head of the Yangtze, you at its tail

meaning.en: The opening of Li Zhiyi's lyric: two people separated by the whole length of a river yet joined by the same water.
meaning.zh: 李之仪词的开篇：两人一个住在江头、一个住在江尾，相隔遥远，却共饮一江水。

equivalents: so far apart, yet under the same sky
a river runs between us

examples.zh: 朋友在信里引用“我住长江头，君住长江尾”，表达对远方爱人的思念。
examples.en: In her letter she quoted 'I live at the head of the Yangtze, you at its tail' to say how she missed her far-off love.

examples.zh: 两地分居的夫妻常用“我住长江头，君住长江尾”自嘲。
examples.en: Couples living apart often joke about it with 'I live at the head of the Yangtze, you at its tail'.

origin.source: 李之仪《卜算子·我住长江头》

story.en: Li Zhiyi (c.1048-1127), a Northern Song poet, wrote the lyric 'Bu Suan Zi'; it runs 'I live at the head of the Yangtze, you at its tail; day after day I think of you but cannot see you, yet we drink the same Yangtze water.'
story.zh: 北宋李之仪（约1048—1127）作《卜算子》：“我住长江头，君住长江尾。日日思君不见君，共饮长江水。”

usage.en: Widely quoted in love letters, songs and captions about long-distance love. Next lines: 日日思君不见君，共饮长江水.
usage.zh: 常见于情书、歌词和异地恋的感慨。下文为“日日思君不见君，共饮长江水”。

text: 只愿君心似我心，定不负相思意
pinyin: zhī yuàn jūn xīn sì wǒ xīn, dìng bù fù xiāng sī yì
literal: only · wish · your · heart · be like · my · heart, surely · not · fail · longing · feeling
natural: I only wish your heart were like mine, then I would not fail your longing

meaning.en: The closing lines of Li Zhiyi's lyric: a wish that the beloved's heart match the speaker's, so that their longing is not in vain.
meaning.zh: 李之仪词的结尾：只希望你的心像我的心一样，这样就不会辜负彼此的相思之情。

equivalents: I only hope you feel as I do
may your heart be as true as mine

examples.zh: 她在贺卡上写下“只愿君心似我心，定不负相思意”。
examples.en: She wrote 'I only wish your heart were like mine, then I would not fail your longing' on the card.

examples.zh: 婚礼上，新郎念出“只愿君心似我心，定不负相思意”。
examples.en: At the wedding the groom read out 'I only wish your heart were like mine, so that I do not fail your longing'.

origin.source: 李之仪《卜算子·我住长江头》

story.en: The final couplet of Li Zhiyi's 'Bu Suan Zi': 'I only wish your heart were like mine, then I would not fail your longing.'
story.zh: 李之仪《卜算子》的结句：“只愿君心似我心，定不负相思意。”

usage.en: A romantic quotation for letters, cards and weddings. Often quoted together with 我住长江头，君住长江尾. Literary.
usage.zh: 情书、贺卡、婚礼上常引的深情之语，常与“我住长江头，君住长江尾”连用。书面。

pinyin: mǎn jiē rén dōu shì shèng rén
literal: full · street · people · all · are · sages
natural: everyone in the street is a sage

meaning.en: Wang Yangming's teaching in a line: every ordinary person has the innate moral knowledge to become a sage.
meaning.zh: 王阳明心学思想的一句话概括：每个普通人都有成圣的良知。

equivalents: everyone has a sage within
every man has it in him to be a saint

examples.zh: 王阳明说“满街人都是圣人”，意思是人人心中都有良知。
examples.en: Wang Yangming said 'everyone in the street is a sage', meaning that everyone has innate moral knowledge.

examples.zh: 老师用“满街人都是圣人”这句话讲解心学的平等观。
examples.en: The teacher used the line 'everyone in the street is a sage' to explain the egalitarian view of the School of Mind.

story.en: In the Instructions for Practical Living (传习录), Wang Ruzhi returns from a walk and reports 'I saw that everyone in the street is a sage'; Wang Yangming answers that the same is true the other way round.
story.zh: 《传习录·下》记王汝止出游而归，说“见满街人都是圣人”，王阳明答以“你看满街人是圣人，满街人倒看你是圣人在”。

usage.en: In the 《传习录》 the words are first spoken by his disciple Wang Ruzhi (王汝止), who says he saw 满街人都是圣人 while out walking; Wang Yangming replies that Ruzhi sees everyone as a sage while everyone sees Ruzhi as one too. Popularly quoted as Wang Yangming's thought.
usage.zh: 《传习录》中，这句话最初是弟子王汝止出游归来所说，王阳明回应说“你看满街人是圣人，满街人倒看你是圣人在”。后世常当作王阳明的思想引用。

text: 不到园林，怎知春色如许
pinyin: bù dào yuán lín, zěn zhī chūn sè rú xǔ
literal: not · reach · garden, how · know · spring · colour · so much
natural: if you never reach the garden, how would you know spring is so lovely?

meaning.en: Du Liniang's cry on seeing the garden in bloom: you cannot know such beauty without going to see it.
meaning.zh: 杜丽娘游园时的感叹：不亲自来到园林，怎知春光如此美好。

equivalents: you have to see it to believe it
you'd never know without going

examples.zh: 春天来了，真应该“不到园林，怎知春色如许”，出去走走吧。
examples.en: Spring is here; as the line says, 'if you never reach the garden, how would you know spring is so lovely?' Let's go out for a walk.

examples.zh: 旅游宣传片用“不到园林，怎知春色如许”做标题。
examples.en: The travel promo used 'if you never reach the garden, how would you know spring is so lovely' as its title.

story.en: In Act 10 of Tang Xianzu's play 'The Peony Pavilion', Du Liniang sees the garden in bloom for the first time and says 'If one never comes to the garden, how would one know spring is so lovely?'
story.zh: 汤显祖《牡丹亭》第十出《惊梦》，杜丽娘初游后花园，见春色满园，感叹“不到园林，怎知春色如许！”

usage.en: Quoted when urging someone to travel or to see something for themselves, especially in spring. Literary; often applied to Suzhou gardens.
usage.zh: 多用于劝人出游、亲眼一见，尤其在春天，常用来形容园林之美。书面。

pinyin: shēng zhě kě yǐ sǐ, sǐ kě yǐ shēng
literal: the living · can · die, the dead · can · live
natural: the living may die, and the dead may live again

meaning.en: Tang Xianzu's description of the power of love: it can make the living die for it and the dead return to life.
meaning.zh: 汤显祖描写情的力量：活着的人可以为情而死，死去的人也可以因情而复生。

equivalents: love conquers even death
love that can raise the dead

examples.zh: 汤显祖说“生者可以死，死可以生”，写尽了至情的力量。
examples.en: Tang Xianzu's 'the living may die, and the dead may live again' sums up the power of true love.

examples.zh: 读完《牡丹亭》，才明白“生者可以死，死可以生”的含义。
examples.en: Only after reading The Peony Pavilion does one grasp what 'the living may die, and the dead may live again' means.

story.en: In his preface to The Peony Pavilion Tang Xianzu writes: 'Love knows not whence it arises, yet once it goes it goes deep; the living may die of it, and the dead may live again.'
story.zh: 汤显祖《牡丹亭题词》：“情不知所起，一往而深，生者可以死，死可以生。”

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of The Peony Pavilion and of passionate love. It follows 情不知所起，一往而深. Literary.
usage.zh: 谈《牡丹亭》和至情时引用，上承“情不知所起，一往而深”。书面。

text: 质本洁来还洁去，强于污淖陷渠沟
pinyin: zhì běn jié lái huán jié qù, qiáng yú wū nào xiàn qú gōu
literal: nature · originally · pure · came · still · pure · go, better than · foul · mud · sink into · ditch
natural: pure by nature, I came pure and will go pure; better that than sinking into a foul ditch

meaning.en: Lin Daiyu's vow in the Burying Flowers Lament: she would rather depart as clean as she came than be stained by the mud of the world.
meaning.zh: 林黛玉《葬花吟》中的名句：宁可干干净净地来、干干净净地去，也不愿陷入污浊的泥沟。

equivalents: better to die pure than live defiled
pure I came, pure I go

examples.zh: 黛玉吟出“质本洁来还洁去，强于污淖陷渠沟”，表明了她的孤高。
examples.en: Daiyu's 'pure I came, pure I go, better than sinking into a foul ditch' shows her proud aloofness.

examples.zh: 他把“质本洁来还洁去，强于污淖陷渠沟”抄在笔记本扉页，作为做人的准则。
examples.en: He copied 'pure I came, pure I go, better than sinking into a foul ditch' onto the flyleaf of his notebook as a rule for how to live.

origin.source: 曹雪芹《红楼梦》第二十七回《葬花吟》

story.en: In chapter 27 of Cao Xueqin's 'Dream of the Red Chamber' Lin Daiyu buries fallen petals and sings the 'Burying Flowers Lament'; its lines include 'Better to wrap the lovely bones in a silk bag and cover them with clean earth; pure I came, pure I go, better than sinking into a foul ditch.'
story.zh: 《红楼梦》第二十七回，林黛玉葬花并吟《葬花吟》，其中有“未若锦囊收艳骨，一抔净土掩风流。质本洁来还洁去，强于污淖陷渠沟”。

usage.en: Quoted for moral integrity and, with the poem's mood, for a delicate, doomed purity. Literary.
usage.zh: 常用来表示操守洁净，也带有《葬花吟》中柔弱而孤高的悲剧色彩。书面。

text: 字字看来皆是血，十年辛苦不寻常
pinyin: zì zì kàn lái jiē shì xuè, shí nián xīn kǔ bù xún cháng
literal: word · word · look · come · all · is · blood, ten · years · toil · not · ordinary
natural: every word you read is blood; ten years of toil was no ordinary effort

meaning.en: A couplet about the painstaking creation of Dream of the Red Chamber: each word cost the author blood and tears over ten years.
meaning.zh: 形容《红楼梦》写作的艰辛：每个字都是心血，十年辛苦非同寻常。

equivalents: every word written in blood
a labour of love over many years

examples.zh: 谈到《红楼梦》的创作，人们常引“字字看来皆是血，十年辛苦不寻常”。
examples.en: Talking about the making of Dream of the Red Chamber, people often quote 'every word is blood, ten years of toil no ordinary effort'.

examples.zh: 这部书稿改了十年，真是字字看来皆是血，十年辛苦不寻常。
examples.en: The manuscript took ten years of revision; truly every word is blood and ten years of toil no ordinary effort.

usage.en: The couplet is traditionally printed with the novel's opening matter, but who wrote it (Cao Xueqin, the commentator Zhiyan Zhai, or a later hand) is not settled, so it is given here as a saying with no fixed source. Also used of any work that took great labour.
usage.zh: 这副对句通常附在《红楼梦》开卷处，但作者是曹雪芹、脂砚斋还是后人，学界并无定论，所以这里作俗语处理，不标出处。也可泛指耗尽心血的作品。

text: 眼中之竹，非胸中之竹也；胸中之竹，又非手中之竹也
pinyin: yǎn zhōng zhī zhú, fēi xiōng zhōng zhī zhú yě, xiōng zhōng zhī zhú, yòu fēi shǒu zhōng zhī zhú yě
literal: eye · in · 's · bamboo, is not · chest · in · 's · bamboo, chest · in · 's · bamboo, also · is not · hand · in · 's · bamboo
natural: the bamboo in the eye is not the bamboo in the mind, and the bamboo in the mind is not the bamboo in the hand

meaning.en: Zheng Banqiao on the stages of artistic creation: what the eye sees, what the mind forms and what the hand paints are three different things.
meaning.zh: 郑板桥谈艺术创作的三个阶段：眼中所见、胸中所构、手下所画，彼此并不相同。

equivalents: from vision to idea to execution
what you see, what you imagine and what you make are three different things

examples.zh: 画家常说“眼中之竹，非胸中之竹也；胸中之竹，又非手中之竹也”，提醒学生创作要经过提炼。
examples.en: Painters often say 'the bamboo in the eye is not the bamboo in the mind, and the bamboo in the mind is not the bamboo in the hand', reminding students that creation needs refining.

examples.zh: 写作课上，老师引用“眼中之竹，非胸中之竹也；胸中之竹，又非手中之竹也”讲构思与表达的差距。
examples.en: In the writing class the teacher quoted 'the bamboo in the eye is not the bamboo in the mind, and the bamboo in the mind is not the bamboo in the hand' on the gap between conception and expression.

usage.en: This is the condensed form in which the passage is usually quoted; Zheng's original is longer, saying that the bamboo in the chest is not the bamboo in the eye, and that once he put brush to paper the bamboo in the hand was again different from that in the chest. It develops the idea behind 胸有成竹, which is traditionally traced to Su Shi's essay on Wen Tong's bamboo paintings. Literary. The wording is a common condensed form of 郑板桥's inscription, not a verbatim quotation.
usage.zh: 这是通行的凝练引法；郑板桥原文较长，说胸中之竹并非眼中之竹，落笔之后手中之竹又不同于胸中之竹。成语“胸有成竹”即与此相关。书面。此为郑板桥题画语的通行概括，并非原文逐字。

story.en: In a painting inscription on bamboo, Zheng Banqiao says the bamboo in his eyes is not the bamboo in his mind, and the bamboo in his mind is not the bamboo under his brush. The entry condenses that account of the stages of creation.
story.zh: 郑板桥题画竹，言眼中之竹非胸中之竹，胸中之竹又非手中之竹，道出艺术创作的几个阶段；此处为凝缩说法。

text: 国家不幸诗家幸，赋到沧桑句便工
pinyin: guó jiā bù xìng shī jiā xìng, fù dào cāng sāng jù biàn gōng
literal: country · not · fortunate · poets · fortunate, speak · reach · vicissitudes · words · only then · fine
natural: misfortune for the state is fortune for the poet: words are finest when they speak of great upheaval

meaning.en: Zhao Yi's verdict on Yuan Haowen: national calamity gives poets their deepest material, and poems about great change reach their highest craft.
meaning.zh: 赵翼评论元好问的名句：国家遭遇不幸，诗人反而得到深刻的创作素材，写到沧桑巨变，诗句才格外工致动人。

equivalents: adversity makes great art
suffering is the poet's gift

examples.zh: 评论家常引用“国家不幸诗家幸，赋到沧桑句便工”来解释乱世出诗人的现象。
examples.en: Critics often use 'misfortune for the state is fortune for the poet; verse grows finest when it sings of upheaval' to explain why troubled times produce poets.

examples.zh: “国家不幸诗家幸，赋到沧桑句便工”，杜甫的诗正是例证。
examples.en: 'Misfortune for the state is fortune for the poet; verse grows finest when it sings of upheaval'; Du Fu's poetry is the proof.

story.en: Zhao Yi (1727-1814) wrote a poem on reading the works of Yuan Haowen (courtesy name Yishan), the Jin-dynasty poet who lived through the Mongol conquest; it ends 'Misfortune for the state is fortune for the poet; words are finest when they speak of great upheaval.'
story.zh: 赵翼（1727—1814）读金代诗人元好问（号遗山）遗集有感而作，诗末云：“国家不幸诗家幸，话到沧桑语始工。”元好问经历了蒙古灭金之乱。

usage.en: From the last couplet of 赵翼《题遗山诗》 on the poet 元好问, who lived through the fall of the Jin. Often quoted to explain why troubled times produce great poetry; sometimes ironic. Literary.
usage.zh: 出自赵翼《题遗山诗》末联，评元好问身经金亡而诗风沉郁。常用来说明乱世出好诗，有时带反讽意味。书面。

text: 等闲变却故人心，却道故人心易变
pinyin: děng xián biàn què gù rén xīn, què dào gù rén xīn yì biàn
literal: casually · change · away · old · friend · heart, yet · say · old · friend · heart · easily · changes
natural: you casually change your old love's heart, then say old hearts change easily

meaning.en: Nalan Xingde's rebuke of a faithless lover: the one who changes first blames the other for being fickle.
meaning.zh: 纳兰性德对薄情者的责备：自己轻易变了心，反倒说旧人的心容易变。

equivalents: blaming the other for your own fickleness
you change, then call me changeable

examples.zh: 她看着他的信，想起“等闲变却故人心，却道故人心易变”。
examples.en: Reading his letter, she thought of the line 'you casually change your old love's heart, then say old hearts change easily'.

examples.zh: 分手后他还怪对方无情，真是等闲变却故人心，却道故人心易变。
examples.en: After the break-up he still blamed her for being cold-hearted; truly 'he changes her heart and says old hearts change easily'.

origin.source: 纳兰性德《木兰花令·拟古决绝词柬友》

story.en: Nalan Xingde (1655-1685) wrote this lyric in the voice of an abandoned woman, sent to a friend; it begins 'If life could only stay as at first meeting, why should autumn wind grieve over the painted fan?' and continues with this couplet.
story.zh: 纳兰性德（1655—1685）以弃妇口吻作此词寄友人，开篇云“人生若只如初见，何事秋风悲画扇”，接着便是此联。

usage.en: Often quoted of someone who is unfaithful yet puts the blame on the other person. It follows the famous 人生若只如初见. Literary.
usage.zh: 常用来说自己变心反而责怪对方的人，上承名句“人生若只如初见”。书面。

text: 谁念西风独自凉，萧萧黄叶闭疏窗，沉思往事立残阳
pinyin: shéi niàn xī fēng dú zì liáng, xiāo xiāo huáng yè bì shū chuāng, chén sī wǎng shì lì cán yáng
literal: who · care · west · wind · alone · cold, rustling · yellow · leaves · shut · sparse · window, ponder · past · events · stand · setting sun
natural: who cares that I shiver alone in the west wind? Yellow leaves rustle outside my shuttered window; I stand in the fading sun, brooding on the past

meaning.en: Nalan Xingde's opening lines, picturing autumn loneliness after the death of his wife: nobody shares his chill, and he can only recall the past.
meaning.zh: 纳兰性德悼念亡妻词的上阕：秋风中无人关心他的孤凉，只能关窗独立，沉思往事。

equivalents: alone in the autumn wind with only memories
who shares my cold?

examples.zh: 深秋的傍晚，他想起“谁念西风独自凉，萧萧黄叶闭疏窗，沉思往事立残阳”。
examples.en: On a late autumn evening he thought of 'who cares that I shiver alone in the west wind? Yellow leaves rustle outside my shuttered window; I stand in the fading sun, brooding on the past'.

examples.zh: 语文课上，老师带大家朗读“谁念西风独自凉，萧萧黄叶闭疏窗，沉思往事立残阳”。
examples.en: In Chinese class the teacher led everyone in reading 'who cares that I shiver alone in the west wind? Yellow leaves rustle outside my shuttered window; I stand in the fading sun, brooding on the past'.

origin.source: 纳兰性德《浣溪沙·谁念西风独自凉》

story.en: Nalan Xingde (1655-1685), the Qing lyricist, wrote this 'Huan Xi Sha'; the first stanza reads 'Who cares that I shiver alone in the west wind? Yellow leaves rustle outside my shuttered window; I stand in the fading sun, brooding on the past.'
story.zh: 清代词人纳兰性德（1655—1685）作《浣溪沙》，上阕为“谁念西风独自凉，萧萧黄叶闭疏窗，沉思往事立残阳”。

usage.en: Quoted for autumn loneliness and grief; usually read as a lament for his wife Lu, though the lyric does not name her. The second half (被酒莫惊春睡重…当时只道是寻常) is an entry of its own.
usage.zh: 用于抒写秋日孤寂和悼亡之情；一般认为是怀念亡妻卢氏，词中并未点名。下阕“被酒莫惊春睡重……当时只道是寻常”另有词条。

text: 风一更，雪一更，聒碎乡心梦不成，故园无此声
pinyin: fēng yī gēng, xuě yī gēng, guō suì xiāng xīn mèng bù chéng, gù yuán wú cǐ shēng
literal: wind · one · watch, snow · one · watch, din · shatter · homesick · heart · dream · not · form, old · home · no · this · sound
natural: wind for one watch, snow for one watch, the din shatters my homesick dreams; back home there is no such sound

meaning.en: Nalan Xingde on a frontier campaign: night-long wind and snow break up his dreams of home, which has no such noise.
meaning.zh: 纳兰性德随扈出塞所作：一夜风雪喧嚣，吵碎了思乡的梦，故乡并没有这样的声音。

equivalents: the howling storm keeps me from dreaming of home
homesick in a night of wind and snow

examples.zh: 出差途中遇上大雪，他想起“风一更，雪一更，聒碎乡心梦不成，故园无此声”。
examples.en: Caught in snow on a business trip, he thought of 'wind for one watch, snow for one watch, the din shatters my homesick dreams; back home there is no such sound'.

examples.zh: 异乡的冬夜里，她轻声念着“风一更，雪一更，聒碎乡心梦不成，故园无此声”。
examples.en: On a winter night far from home she murmured 'wind for one watch, snow for one watch, the din shatters my homesick dreams; back home there is no such sound'.

origin.source: 纳兰性德《长相思·山一程》

story.en: Nalan Xingde (1655-1685) wrote 'Chang Xiang Si' while accompanying the Kangxi emperor beyond the Shanhai Pass in 1682; it begins 'A stretch of mountains, a stretch of water, I travel toward the pass; deep in the night a thousand tents glow with lamps', then continues with these lines.
story.zh: 康熙二十一年（1682）纳兰性德随康熙帝出山海关，作《长相思》，上阕“山一程，水一程，身向榆关那畔行，夜深千帐灯”，下阕即此数句。

usage.en: Quoted for homesickness on a cold night. A 更 is one of the five night watches, roughly two hours. Literary.
usage.zh: 用于寒夜思乡。一更指夜间五更之一，约两小时。书面。

text: 若似月轮终皎洁，不辞冰雪为卿热
pinyin: ruò sì yuè lún zhōng jiǎo jié, bù cí bīng xuě wèi qīng rè
literal: if · be like · moon · wheel · in the end · bright and pure, not · decline · ice · snow · for · you · warm
natural: if you could be as bright as the full moon, I would gladly burn with warmth through ice and snow for you

meaning.en: Nalan Xingde's pledge of devotion: if the beloved could stay as pure as the moon, he would warm her even through ice and snow.
meaning.zh: 纳兰性德表达深情的词句：如果你能像圆月一样始终皎洁，我愿冒冰雪严寒，为你燃起热情。

equivalents: I'd brave ice and snow for you
devotion through hardship

examples.zh: 他在纪念册上写下“若似月轮终皎洁，不辞冰雪为卿热”。
examples.en: He wrote 'if you could be as bright as the full moon, I would gladly burn with warmth through ice and snow for you' in the memory book.

examples.zh: 朗诵会上，她深情地读了“若似月轮终皎洁，不辞冰雪为卿热”。
examples.en: At the poetry reading she recited 'if you could be as bright as the full moon, I would gladly burn with warmth through ice and snow for you' with deep feeling.

origin.source: 纳兰性德《蝶恋花·辛苦最怜天上月》

story.en: The lyric begins 'Most pitiable is the moon in heaven, toiling, one night a ring, night after night a broken one', and ends with this couplet.
story.zh: 此词开篇为“辛苦最怜天上月，一昔如环，昔昔都成玦”，结句即此联。

usage.en: Quoted as a declaration of love and loyalty. In the original lyric it is a wish against the moon's waxing and waning. Literary.
usage.zh: 用作爱情和忠贞的表白。原词是对月亮圆缺的感慨之语。书面。

text: 慎独则心安，主敬则身强，求仁则人悦，习劳则神钦
pinyin: shèn dú zé xīn ān, zhǔ jìng zé shēn qiáng, qiú rén zé rén yuè, xí láo zé shén qīn
literal: be watchful alone · then · heart · at ease, hold reverence · then · body · strong, seek humaneness · then · people · pleased, practise labour · then · spirits · respect
natural: be watchful in solitude and the heart is at peace; hold to reverence and the body is strong; seek humaneness and people are glad; practise hard work and the spirits approve

meaning.en: The four daily rules of Zeng Guofan for self-cultivation: integrity in private, reverence, kindness and diligence.
meaning.zh: 曾国藩的修身“日课四条”：独处时谨慎自律，心才安稳；保持敬畏，身体才强健；以仁待人，别人才喜悦；勤于劳作，神明也钦佩。

equivalents: integrity, reverence, kindness and hard work
four rules for a well-lived life

examples.zh: 他把“慎独则心安，主敬则身强，求仁则人悦，习劳则神钦”当作修身的座右铭。
examples.en: He took 'be watchful in solitude and the heart is at peace; hold to reverence and the body is strong; seek humaneness and people are glad; practise hard work and the spirits approve' as his motto of self-cultivation.

examples.zh: 讲座介绍曾国藩的家训，其中就有“慎独则心安，主敬则身强，求仁则人悦，习劳则神钦”。
examples.en: The lecture on Zeng Guofan's family teachings included 'be watchful in solitude and the heart is at peace; hold to reverence and the body is strong; seek humaneness and people are glad; practise hard work and the spirits approve'.

story.en: Zeng Guofan (1811-1872), the Qing statesman and Xiang Army commander, set himself 'four daily lessons' and passed them on in his family letters: 一曰慎独则心安，二曰主敬则身强，三曰求仁则人悦，四曰习劳则神钦.
story.zh: 清代政治家、湘军统帅曾国藩（1811—1872）订有“日课四条”，并在家书中告诫子弟：“一曰慎独则心安，二曰主敬则身强，三曰求仁则人悦，四曰习劳则神钦。”

usage.en: Usually quoted as the 日课四条 (Four Daily Lessons). Often given in the shortened forms 慎独 or 习劳. Formal; popular in self-improvement writing.
usage.zh: 通常称“日课四条”，也常简称其中的“慎独”“习劳”。正式，常见于修身励志类文章。

text: 有牛之体，则有负重之用；有马之体，则有致远之用；未闻以牛为体，以马为用者也
pinyin: yǒu niú zhī tǐ, zé yǒu fù zhòng zhī yòng, yǒu mǎ zhī tǐ, zé yǒu zhì yuǎn zhī yòng, wèi wén yǐ niú wéi tǐ, yǐ mǎ wéi yòng zhě yě
literal: have · ox · 's · substance, then · have · load-bearing · 's · function, have · horse · 's · substance, then · have · far-reaching · 's · function, not · heard · take · ox · as · substance, take · horse · as · function
natural: an ox's body brings the power to carry loads, a horse's body the power to go far; never has one heard of taking the ox as the body and the horse as the function

meaning.en: Yan Fu's rebuttal of the slogan 'Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for use': every body has its own function, and the two cannot be mixed like that.
meaning.zh: 严复批驳“中学为体，西学为用”的论证：每种“体”有自己的“用”，不能把牛的体配上马的用。

equivalents: you can't graft a horse's strength onto an ox
form and function belong together

examples.zh: 讨论“中体西用”时，学者常引用严复的“有牛之体，则有负重之用；有马之体，则有致远之用；未闻以牛为体，以马为用者也”。
examples.en: In discussing 'Chinese learning as essence, Western learning for use', scholars often cite Yan Fu's 'an ox's body brings the power to carry loads, a horse's body the power to go far; never has one heard of taking the ox as the body and the horse as the function'.

examples.zh: 课上老师用“有牛之体，则有负重之用；有马之体，则有致远之用；未闻以牛为体，以马为用者也”说明体用不可分割。
examples.en: In class the teacher used 'an ox's body brings the power to carry loads, a horse's body the power to go far; never has one heard of taking the ox as the body and the horse as the function' to show that essence and function cannot be separated.

story.en: In a 1902 letter to the editor of the Waijiao Bao, Yan Fu (1854-1921), translator of Huxley and Adam Smith, argued that Chinese and Western learning each have their own 'substance' and 'function', and that the formula 'Chinese substance, Western function' is therefore illogical.
story.zh: 严复（1854—1921）1902年写信给《外交报》主人，认为中学西学各有体用，“中学为体、西学为用”的说法在逻辑上讲不通。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of modernisation and of the late-Qing slogan 中体西用. 体 and 用 are philosophical terms (substance and function). Literary and scholarly.
usage.zh: 谈论现代化和晚清“中体西用”口号时引用。“体”“用”是哲学术语，指本体与作用。书面、学术性强。

text: 鹰隼试翼，风尘吸张；奇花初胎，矞矞皇皇；干将发硎，有作其芒
pinyin: yīng sǔn shì yì, fēng chén xī zhāng, qí huā chū tāi, yù yù huáng huáng, gàn jiāng fā xíng, yǒu zuò qí máng
literal: eagle · falcon · try · wings, wind · dust · stirred · spread, rare · flower · first · bud, radiant · radiant, Ganjiang sword · begin · whetstone, show · its · edge
natural: the young hawk tries its wings and the wind and dust are stirred; the rare flower first buds in glorious splendour; the Ganjiang sword leaves the whetstone and its edge begins to shine

meaning.en: Three images from Liang Qichao's 'Young China': the new, young China is a hawk testing its wings, a rare flower in bud and a freshly sharpened sword.
meaning.zh: 梁启超《少年中国说》中的三个比喻：少年中国像刚试飞的鹰隼、初绽的奇花、刚磨好的宝剑，充满生机和锋芒。

equivalents: youth is a hawk on its first flight
a bright future just beginning

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长朗诵“鹰隼试翼，风尘吸张；奇花初胎，矞矞皇皇；干将发硎，有作其芒”，勉励青年人。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the principal recited 'the young hawk tries its wings and the wind and dust are stirred; the rare flower first buds in glorious splendour; the Ganjiang sword leaves the whetstone and its edge begins to shine' to encourage the young.

examples.zh: 同学们在作文里引用“鹰隼试翼，风尘吸张；奇花初胎，矞矞皇皇；干将发硎，有作其芒”来赞美青春。
examples.en: In their essays the students quoted 'the young hawk tries its wings and the wind and dust are stirred; the rare flower first buds in glorious splendour; the Ganjiang sword leaves the whetstone and its edge begins to shine' in praise of youth.

story.en: Liang Qichao (1873-1929) published 'Young China' in 1900 in Yokohama, in answer to the Western label of China as an 'old, decaying empire'; he contrasts old age with the energy of youth and ends with a run of images of rising life.
story.zh: 梁启超（1873—1929）1900年在日本横滨发表《少年中国说》，反驳西方称中国为“老大帝国”，以少年的朝气对比老朽，文末连用一串新生事物的比喻。

usage.en: A set piece of school recitation and essays; 矞 is read yù and 硎 is read xíng. It sits in the middle of a run of images ending 前途似海，来日方长. Literary and rousing.
usage.zh: 学校朗诵和作文的常用段落；“矞”读yù，“硎”读xíng。位于一连串比喻之间，后接“前途似海，来日方长”。书面，慷慨激昂。

text: 人生须知负责任的苦处，才能知道尽责任的乐趣
pinyin: rén shēng xū zhī fù zé rèn de kǔ chù, cái néng zhī dào jìn zé rèn de lè qù
literal: life · must · know · bear · responsibility · 's · bitterness, only then · can · know · fulfil · responsibility · 's · joy
natural: one must know the bitterness of bearing responsibility before one can know the joy of discharging it

meaning.en: Liang Qichao's thesis in 'The Greatest Pain and the Greatest Joy': the greatest suffering is an unfulfilled duty and the greatest joy is a duty done.
meaning.zh: 梁启超《最苦与最乐》的核心观点：人最苦的是有责任未了，最乐的是责任尽完；要先尝到负责任的苦，才懂尽责任的乐。

equivalents: no pain, no gain
duty done is the sweetest rest

examples.zh: 毕业了才明白“人生须知负责任的苦处，才能知道尽责任的乐趣”。
examples.en: Only after graduation did I understand that 'one must know the bitterness of bearing responsibility before one can know the joy of discharging it'.

examples.zh: 老师在班会上引用“人生须知负责任的苦处，才能知道尽责任的乐趣”，鼓励大家承担班级工作。
examples.en: At the class meeting the teacher quoted 'one must know the bitterness of bearing responsibility before one can know the joy of discharging it' to encourage everyone to take on class duties.

story.en: In this essay, a talk to students given in 1912 after his return from exile, Liang Qichao (1873-1929) argues that responsibility brings pain while it is unfulfilled and joy when it is fulfilled.
story.zh: 梁启超（1873—1929）1912年归国后对学生演讲的文章《最苦与最乐》，论述责任未尽时是苦，尽了责任则是乐。

usage.en: A school-textbook favourite, used in essays and talks on duty and growing up. The essay's thesis is that 'the greatest pain is unfulfilled duty, the greatest joy is duty done'.
usage.zh: 学校课本常选，作文和讲话中常用于谈责任与成长。文章的主旨是“人生最苦的事，莫苦于身上背着一种未了的责任；人生最快乐的事，莫快乐于自己对自己所负的责任完全解除”。

text: 杜鹃再拜忧天泪，精卫无穷填海心
pinyin: dù juān zài bài yōu tiān lèi, jīng wèi wú qióng tián hǎi xīn
literal: cuckoo · again · bow · worry · heaven · tears, Jingwei bird · endless · fill · sea · heart
natural: the cuckoo bows again, weeping over the sky; the Jingwei bird has an endless heart for filling the sea

meaning.en: Huang Zunxian's couplet to Liang Qichao: a patriot's tears for the nation's fate, and the stubborn will of the bird that fills the sea with pebbles.
meaning.zh: 黄遵宪赠梁启超的联句：像杜鹃一样为国家命运泣血忧虑，像精卫一样矢志不渝、永不放弃。

equivalents: tears for the nation and a will that never tires
persevering against hopeless odds

examples.zh: 教授引用“杜鹃再拜忧天泪，精卫无穷填海心”来形容近代知识分子的家国情怀。
examples.en: The professor quoted 'the cuckoo bows again, weeping over the sky; the Jingwei bird has an endless heart for filling the sea' to describe modern intellectuals' devotion to country.

examples.zh: 他把“杜鹃再拜忧天泪，精卫无穷填海心”写成对联挂在书房。
examples.en: He wrote 'the cuckoo bows again, weeping over the sky; the Jingwei bird has an endless heart for filling the sea' as a couplet and hung it in his study.

story.en: Huang Zunxian (1848-1905), diplomat and poet of the 'new-style poetry' movement, addressed this poem to Liang Qichao (courtesy name Renfu); it begins 'Every inch of land is worth an inch of gold; who can bear the burden of its being split and torn?'
story.zh: 黄遵宪（1848—1905）为外交官、“诗界革命”代表诗人，赠梁启超（字任父）此诗，开头为“寸寸河山寸寸金，侉离分裂力谁任”。

usage.en: Quoted for patriotic sorrow and perseverance. The cuckoo (杜鹃) is a classical symbol of grief and 精卫 is the mythical bird that tried to fill the sea (see 精卫填海). Literary.
usage.zh: 用于抒发忧国之情和坚持不懈的志向。杜鹃是古典诗词中悲啼的象征，精卫是传说中衔石填海的神鸟（见“精卫填海”）。书面。
